fold-a-batch-of-registry-requests-within.text: Fold a batch of registry requests within measured network limits.

Issue 746, part of epic 731. This page is for a folder (anyone who wants to fold a registry's pending requests), for the integrators who run folders, and for the people who review the pull requests. It records the story, the requirements, the refusals and the checks that prove them. It follows the reader ticket and the update and termination ticket.

story.text: As a folder, I give a network and a registry's name, and a wallet that booked none of the requests finds the registry's pending registrations and terminations from public data, folds as many as fit in one transaction, keeps what each request holds above what the application requires to stay, and knows from published measurement how large a batch the network accepts.

what-the-folder-finds-and-takes.text: What the folder finds and takes.

requirements.text: batch-follows-the-model: the batch fold implements the statements of the plan's Lean binding; each refusal and each success has an executable check seen to fail.

pending-found-from-public-data: the pending requests of a registry are found from the provider alone, by the approvals under the application policy and their holders; a wallet that booked none of them finds the same set as the booker.

foreign-holders-skipped: a request held at a key address, a request of another registry and an undecodable output are skipped and named, each beside a control that folds the same shape when it is held correctly.

unfoldable-requests-skipped: in automatic selection a request the builder would refuse on its own account is skipped and named, never handed to the builder; the first individually foldable request for a key in the order keeps it; every discovered request is folded, skipped with its reason or counted as left, and a skipped one is never counted as left; each class has a control that folds the same shape when it is foldable.
mixed-batch: one transaction folds registrations and terminations of one registry together.
folder-takes-the-surplus: the transaction's change carries each request's value above what the application requires to stay, read from the chain and not from a command's receipt.

largest-fitting-batch: when more requests are pending than fit, the fold takes the largest ordered prefix the network accepts and reports the count left; it never refuses only because more are pending, and a failure that is not a capacity limit is never read as "does not fit".

batch-refusals: a named batch with a request of another registry, a named batch with a duplicate key, and a batch that moves anything else under the state policy are each refused, beside an accepted control.

limits-measured: a measurement receipt binds the exact scripts, the workload and the protocol parameters, and states the largest accepted batch for registrations, terminations and mixed batches, with memory, steps, bytes and fee per request.
limits-stated-as-measured: every published limit names the receipt it comes from and the workload it was measured on; none is typed.
devnet-batch-journey: on a development network, through the packaged commands, a wallet that booked none of the requests discovers and folds a mixed batch of one registry.
documentation-and-conformance: the user documentation describes folding and its limits, and the conformance suite carries the batch rows, in the same change.
hosted-checks-green: hosted checks green on each pull request into main.

what-the-receipt-and-the-documentation-c.text: What the receipt and the documentation claim.

The measurement shows what one network accepted for one workload under one set of protocol parameters. It claims nothing about a larger registry, a different trie depth, other scripts or other parameters; the receipt names each, and the documentation repeats the numbers from the receipt. The trie library's proofs are assumed sound.

out-of-scope.text: Folds of several registries in one transaction, the reader (issue 744), integration and release (issue 747), general capacity work (issue 530). Ordering by anything but the folder's take is not a goal of this ticket.
